## Overview

[eBird Status and Trends](https://science.ebird.org/en/status-and-trends)
provides modeled estimates of species distribution, relative abundance, and
population trend, derived from eBird checklists and remotely sensed habitat
covariates. Unlike the raw eBird observations used elsewhere in this package
(`klamath_ebird`), these are effort-corrected model predictions on a
regular grid, which makes them comparable across space rather than a
reflection of where birders happened to go.

This document pulls two distinct products and clips both to the Klamath
Basin boundary (`rivermile::klamath_hucs`):

1.  **Status** — weekly relative abundance, count, and occurrence rasters
    (3 km resolution).
2.  **Trends** — modeled percent-per-year change in relative abundance
    (~27 km resolution), for 2012-2022.

```{r versions}
ebirdst_version()
```

Note that the status and trends products are on **different release
cycles** — the status estimates and the trends estimates are not from the
same model year, so they should not be described as a single vintage.

### Access key

Status and Trends data require a free access key, requested at
<https://ebird.org/st/request>. The key is a secret and should never be
typed into a chunk, script, or anything that gets committed. Run this once,
directly in the R console (not in this document):

```r
ebirdst::set_ebirdst_access_key("your-key-here")
```

That call writes `EBIRDST_KEY` into `~/.Renviron`, outside the project
directory. From then on every R session — including this document — picks
the key up automatically from the environment, so nothing in this file ever
needs to reference it directly. (The console command itself still lands in
your R history, so if that's a concern, edit `~/.Renviron` directly instead
of using the helper.)

## Study area

`rivermile::klamath_hucs` supplies the Klamath Basin outline used to clip the
rasters and draw the maps.

```{r study-area}
klamath_hucs <- rivermile::klamath_hucs
klamath_outline <- st_union(klamath_hucs)

glimpse(klamath_hucs)
```

Status values are summarized by wildlife refuge using
`rivermile::klamath_refuges`, buffered 0.5 miles and named to match `area` in
`klamath_ebird` and `piscivorous_waterbirds` (the same convention as
`bird_data_synthesis.Rmd`).

```{r study-area-refuges}
refuge_buffer_dist <- units::set_units(0.5, "mi")

klamath_refuges <- rivermile::klamath_refuges |>
  mutate(
    site = case_when(
      str_detect(orgname, "bear valley")   ~ "Bear Valley",
      str_detect(orgname, "clear lake")    ~ "Clear Lake",
      str_detect(orgname, "klamath marsh") ~ "Klamath Marsh",
      str_detect(orgname, "lower klamath") ~ "Lower Klamath - Sheepy",
      str_detect(orgname, "tule lake")     ~ "Tule Lake",
      str_detect(orgname, "upper klamath") ~ "Upper Klamath Lake"
    )
  ) |>
  select(site, orgname) |>
  st_buffer(dist = refuge_buffer_dist)

glimpse(klamath_refuges)
```

Both Status and Trends products are distributed on global equal-area grids,
but not the same one — status rasters are Equal Earth
(EPSG:8857) while the trends grid is sinusoidal. Rather than hard-coding
either, the boundary is reprojected to whatever CRS the downloaded product
reports. Reprojecting the vector rather than the raster matters: warping
the raster would resample the estimates and distort the equal-area cells
that the abundance values are defined on.

## Species

The focal species here are the three tracked by the multispecies subgroup.
`ebirdst_runs` is the authoritative list of what is modeled, including
whether a species has trends estimates at all.

```{r species}
focal_species <- c("Cinnamon Teal", "Eared Grebe", "White-faced Ibis")

focal_runs <- ebirdst_runs |>
  filter(common_name %in% focal_species) |>
  glimpse()

knitr::kable(focal_runs |> 
               select(
                 common_name, species_code, is_resident,
                 breeding_quality, nonbreeding_quality,
                 has_trends, trends_season, trends_start_year, trends_end_year
               ), caption = "Status and Trends model coverage for the focal species")
```

Two things to note before going further:

-   **Eared Grebe has no trends estimates** (`has_trends = FALSE`), so it
    appears in the status section but drops out of the trends section. Any
    species list used here should be filtered on `has_trends` rather than
    assumed complete.
-   Model quality is rated per season on a 0-3 scale. These ratings should
    be checked before interpreting a surface, or the weekly values that
    fall in that season; a low rating means the model was poorly validated
    for that season.

## Status: weekly relative abundance, count, and occurrence

eBird Status models are fit to eBird checklists and environmental covariates,
adjusted for observer effort, and predict for each of 52 weeks on a global
grid what a standardized checklist would record: a 2 km, 1 hour Traveling
Count by an expert observer, at the best time of day for the species. Three
products are pulled, each the weekly median estimate, with
`load_raster(period = "weekly")`:

| `product`    | Cell value                                                 |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `occurrence` | probability (0-1) that the species is reported             |
| `count`      | expected count, *given* that the species occurs            |
| `abundance`  | expected relative abundance, defined as occurrence × count |

```{r status-pull}
# Each 3 km weekly file is global (nine here); use "9km" or "27km" to download less.
status_resolution <- "3km"
status_products <- c("abundance", "count", "occurrence")

#' Load one weekly status product for a species and clip it to the Klamath Basin
clip_status_to_klamath <- function(species, product, resolution = status_resolution) {
  r <- load_raster(
    species,
    product    = product,
    period     = "weekly",
    resolution = resolution
  )

  # Reproject the boundary into the raster's own CRS, not the reverse.
  boundary <- st_transform(klamath_outline, terra::crs(r)) |> vect()

  r |>
    terra::crop(boundary) |>
    terra::mask(boundary)
}

# One pull per species x product, each kept as a 52-layer clipped raster.
status_weekly <- expand_grid(common_name = focal_species, product = status_products) |>
  mutate(raster = map2(common_name, product, clip_status_to_klamath))

# Every pull should return the full 52 weeks.
status_weekly |>
  mutate(
    n_weeks    = map_int(raster, terra::nlyr),
    first_week = map_chr(raster, \(r) names(r)[1]),
    last_week  = map_chr(raster, \(r) names(r)[terra::nlyr(r)])
  ) |>
  select(-raster)
```

Maps use eBird's seasonal mean of weekly abundance (four panels per species);
`ebird_status` itself is built from the weekly pulls.

```{r status-maps, fig.height=8}
display_crs <- "EPSG:32610"
display_buffer <- units::set_units(15, "km")

plot_status <- function(species, resolution = status_resolution) {
  r <- load_raster(
    species,
    product    = "abundance",
    period     = "seasonal",
    metric     = "mean",
    resolution = resolution
  )

  # Loose crop, still in the native CRS, just to keep the reprojection cheap.
  wide_boundary <- st_buffer(klamath_outline, display_buffer) |>
    st_transform(terra::crs(r)) |>
    vect()
  r_wide <- terra::crop(r, wide_boundary)

  # Reproject before the tight crop - see note above.
  r_disp <- terra::project(r_wide, display_crs, method = "bilinear")

  # Only now compute the tight boundary, directly in the display CRS.
  tight_boundary <- st_transform(klamath_outline, display_crs) |> vect()
  r_disp <- r_disp |> terra::crop(tight_boundary) |> terra::mask(tight_boundary)

  ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data = r_disp) +
    geom_sf(data = st_transform(klamath_hucs, display_crs),
            fill = NA, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.25) +
    facet_wrap(~ lyr) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = ebirdst_palettes(20, type = "weekly"),
      na.value = "transparent",
      name = "Relative\nabundance"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = species,
      subtitle = paste0("Seasonal mean relative abundance, ", status_resolution,
                        " resolution, clipped to the Klamath Basin")
    ) +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
}

walk(focal_species, \(sp) print(plot_status(sp)))
```

### How `ebird_status` is calculated

1.  Each species × product pull is a 52-layer raster, one layer per week,
    cropped and masked to the basin.
2.  For each refuge and week, `mean_value` is the mean of the cell values whose
    centre falls inside the refuge (0.5-mile buffer). Cells with no estimate
    are ignored; a refuge with none is `NA`.
3.  The species × product × refuge × week rows are bound into one table.

### What `mean_value` means

-   **`abundance`**: relative to the standardized checklist — not a density or
    a number of birds. Compare across weeks or refuges for one species, not
    between species (see Caveats); don't sum.
-   **`count`**: same scale caveat. Every cell is weighted equally, including
    cells where the species is unlikely, so it is not the count where the
    species is actually found.
-   **`occurrence`**: the average probability of reporting the species at a
    random spot in the refuge, not the probability it occurs somewhere in it.
-   `abundance` is occurrence × count in each cell, but only approximately,
    since each weekly layer is its own median estimate.
-   `week` is the middle date of each week. Its year (2023) is the release's
    prediction year, so read it as a position in the annual cycle.

```{r ebird-status}
#' Mean of every weekly layer within each refuge, long: one row per refuge x week
summarise_by_refuge <- function(r, species, status_product) {
  refuges_prj <- st_transform(klamath_refuges, terra::crs(r))

  terra::extract(r, vect(refuges_prj), fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    bind_cols(area = refuges_prj$site) |>
    pivot_longer(-area, names_to = "week", values_to = "mean_value") |>
    mutate(
      common_name = species,
      product     = status_product,
      # Layer names are the week-midpoint dates.
      week        = as.Date(week),
      # A refuge with no estimated cell (outside the modeled range) is NaN.
      mean_value  = if_else(is.nan(mean_value), NA_real_, mean_value)
    )
}

ebird_status <- status_weekly |>
  pmap(\(common_name, product, raster) summarise_by_refuge(raster, common_name, product)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  select(common_name, product, area, week, mean_value) 
```

```{r status-tables}
ebird_status |>
  filter(product == "abundance", !is.na(mean_value)) |>
  slice_max(mean_value, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = c(common_name, area)) |>
  transmute(
    common_name, area,
    peak_week      = format(week, "%b %d"),
    peak_abundance = mean_value
  ) |>
  arrange(common_name, desc(peak_abundance)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Species", "Refuge", "Peak week", "Peak abundance"),
    caption = "Week of peak mean relative abundance, by wildlife refuge"
  )
```

```{r status-refuge-plot, fig.height=7}
status_pal <- c("Cinnamon Teal" = "#2a78d6", "Eared Grebe" = "#eb6834",
                "White-faced Ibis" = "#1baf7a")

# Occurrence is a probability, count and abundance are on different scales, so
# each product gets its own y-axis.
ebird_status |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_value)) |>
  mutate(product = factor(product, levels = status_products)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = mean_value, color = common_name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(
    product ~ area, scales = "free_y",
    labeller = labeller(area = label_wrap_gen(12))
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b") +
  scale_color_manual(values = status_pal, name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly occurrence, count, and abundance by refuge",
    subtitle = "Same six refuges used for `area` in klamath_ebird and piscivorous_waterbirds",
    x = NULL, y = "Mean value (scale differs by row)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Save Data Object

```{r}
ebird_status |> glimpse()

usethis::use_data(ebird_status, overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Trends: percent change per year

Trends are estimated differently from status. Rather than modeling absolute
abundance in a single year, the trends model finds pairs of checklists that
are close in location and similar in habitat and survey effort but taken in
different years, and asks how relative abundance differed between the two
years of each pair. Averaging that year-over-year change across many such
pairs within a grid cell yields a percent-per-year trend for the cell, along
with a confidence interval. Because it relies on paired comparisons rather
than a single-year surface, this product is modeled on a coarser (~27 km)
grid than status, and only for the 2012-2022 breeding season here. Trend
estimates arrive as a data frame of grid cell centres with
longitude/latitude in EPSG:4326, so the clip is a spatial filter of points
rather than a raster mask.

```{r trends-download}
trends_species <- focal_runs |>
  filter(has_trends) |>
  pull(common_name)

trends_species

walk(trends_species, ebirdst_download_trends)
```

```{r trends-clip}
trends_raw <- set_names(trends_species) |>
  map(\(sp) load_trends(sp)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "common_name")

# Cell centres are lon/lat, so filter in 4326 against the basin outline.
trends_sf <- trends_raw |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

trends_klamath <- trends_sf |>
  st_filter(st_transform(klamath_outline, 4326), .predicate = st_intersects)

# How many 27 km cells actually fall inside the basin?
trends_klamath |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(common_name, season, name = "n_cells")
```

```{r trends-map, fig.height=6}
# ebirdst's own trends palette runs red (decline) -> white (no change) ->
# blue (increase). Keep that direction: it is the convention every published
# Status and Trends map uses, and flipping it would invert the reading.
trends_pal <- ebirdst_palettes(3, type = "trends")

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = st_transform(klamath_hucs, 4326), fill = "grey94", color = "grey70",
          linewidth = 0.25) +
  # shape 21 keeps near-zero (near-white) cells visible against the basin.
  geom_sf(data = trends_klamath, aes(fill = abd_ppy),
          shape = 21, color = "grey35", stroke = 0.3, size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ common_name) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = trends_pal[1], mid = trends_pal[2], high = trends_pal[3],
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "% change\nper year"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Modeled population trend within the Klamath Basin",
    subtitle = "Percent change per year in breeding-season relative abundance, 2012-2022",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
```

A diverging scale centred on zero is used deliberately: the quantity has a
meaningful neutral point (no change), and the two arms read as opposite
directions — **red is decline, blue is increase**, following eBird's own
convention. Cell-level estimates carry wide confidence intervals, so the
summary below reports them rather than the point estimate alone.

```{r trends-summary}
trends_klamath |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(
    n_cells         = n(),
    median_ppy      = median(abd_ppy),
    mean_ppy        = mean(abd_ppy),
    median_ppy_low  = median(abd_ppy_lower),
    median_ppy_high = median(abd_ppy_upper),
    cells_declining = sum(abd_ppy < 0),
    .by = c(common_name, season)
  ) |>
  arrange(median_ppy) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Trend summary for cells intersecting the Klamath Basin")
```

Assigning trend cells to individual subbasins is possible but marginal at
this resolution: a single 27 km cell is comparable in size to the smaller
HUC8s, so a per-subbasin trend would mostly reflect which cell centre landed
where. Basin-wide summaries are the appropriate grain for this product.

### `ebird_trends`: trends by refuge

`ebird_trends` mirrors `ebird_status`: long format, one row per species × metric
× refuge, with `area` matching `klamath_ebird$area`. Each cell has a single
estimate for the breeding season over the full 2012-2022 window of the current
Trends release, and there is no year-by-year series, so `start_year` and
`end_year` take the place of `week`. Eared Grebe has no trends and is excluded.

It follows eBird's regional-trend method (abundance-weighted, computed per
ensemble fold), adapted so each cell counts in proportion to how much of it the
refuge covers:

1.  For each refuge, find the 27 km cells it overlaps and the share of each cell
    it covers.
2.  In each of the 100 ensemble folds, the refuge's `abd_ppy` is
    sum(overlap × `abd` × `abd_ppy`) / sum(overlap × `abd`) over those cells.
3.  `abd_ppy` is the median across folds; `abd_ppy_lower` and `abd_ppy_upper` are
    the 10th and 90th percentiles (an 80% interval).
4.  `abd` is the overlap-weighted mean of the cells' relative abundance at the
    middle of the trend period.

`abd_ppy` is the percent change in relative abundance per year; negative is a
decline. Averaging cell-level interval bounds would not give a valid refuge
interval, which is why folds are used. A 27 km cell (about 711 km²) is far larger
than a refuge (34-325 km²), and each refuge overlaps only 2-4 cells, so the
values describe the surrounding landscape more than the refuge itself.

```{r ebird-trends}
#' Refuge-level trend for one species, from the 27 km cell and fold estimates
trends_by_refuge <- function(species) {
  cells <- load_trends(species)
  folds <- load_trends(species, fold_estimates = TRUE)

  # Raster of cell ids on the trends grid, to get each refuge's overlap with
  # each cell.
  grid <- rasterize_trends(cells, layers = "abd", trim = FALSE)
  cell_ids <- vect(
    cells[c("longitude", "latitude", "srd_id")],
    geom = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = "epsg:4326"
  ) |>
    terra::project(terra::crs(grid)) |>
    terra::rasterize(grid, field = "srd_id")
  names(cell_ids) <- "srd_id"  # rasterize() names the layer "last"

  # Share of each cell covered by each refuge.
  overlap <- terra::extract(
    cell_ids, vect(st_transform(klamath_refuges, terra::crs(grid))),
    exact = TRUE, ID = TRUE
  ) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    filter(!is.na(srd_id)) |>
    transmute(area = klamath_refuges$site[ID], srd_id, weight = fraction)

  # A cell can overlap more than one refuge, hence many-to-many.
  ppy <- folds |>
    inner_join(overlap, by = "srd_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    summarise(ppy = sum(weight * abd * abd_ppy) / sum(weight * abd), .by = c(area, fold)) |>
    summarise(
      abd_ppy       = median(ppy),
      abd_ppy_lower = quantile(ppy, 0.1, names = FALSE),
      abd_ppy_upper = quantile(ppy, 0.9, names = FALSE),
      .by = area
    )

  abd <- cells |>
    inner_join(overlap, by = "srd_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    summarise(abd = sum(weight * abd) / sum(weight), .by = area)

  full_join(ppy, abd, by = "area") |>
    mutate(
      common_name = species,
      season      = cells$season[1],
      start_year  = cells$start_year[1],
      end_year    = cells$end_year[1]
    )
}

ebird_trends <- trends_species |>
  map(trends_by_refuge) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(abd_ppy, abd_ppy_lower, abd_ppy_upper, abd),
    names_to = "metric", values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  select(common_name, metric, area, season, start_year, end_year, value) |>
  glimpse()

usethis::use_data(ebird_trends, overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Caveats

-   **Model output, not observation.** These are predictions from a model
    fit to eBird data. They are effort-corrected, which is precisely why
    they are useful alongside `klamath_ebird`, but they inherit the
    assumptions of the underlying model.
-   **Don't compare relative abundance between species.** eBird advises
    against it "because the percentages of undetected individuals will differ
    among species" ([eBird Status and Trends
    FAQ](https://science.ebird.org/status-and-trends/faq#abundance)). Compare
    one species across weeks or refuges. The plots draw species together for
    layout only.
-   **Check seasonal quality ratings.** A season rated 0-1 should not be
    interpreted, and that applies to the weeks that fall inside it. The
    species table above shows each season's rating, and `ebirdst_runs`
    gives the season dates, which are not carried in `ebird_status`.
-   **Resolution mismatch.** Status is clipped at 3 km, trends at ~27 km.
    The two are not directly comparable cell-for-cell, and the basin
    contains relatively few trend cells.
-   **Small refuges.** Each refuge mean uses the 3 km cells whose centre falls
    inside the buffered refuge, so cells straddling the edge are in or out
    whole. Refuges are small relative to that grid: Bear Valley has only
    about 3 such cells (about 34 km² with the buffer), versus roughly 20-37
    for the other five, so its mean in particular is indicative rather than
    precise.
-   **Trends are breeding-season only** for these species, so they say
    nothing about the migratory and wintering periods that the status
    surfaces do cover.

Data products must be cited; `ebirdst` bundles the current citation.

```{r citation, eval=FALSE}
citation("ebirdst")
```
